Eccentric

/ik-SEN-trik/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Eccentric means unconventional or slightly strange in behavior or personal habits, usually in a harmless or endearing way.

Our eccentric neighbor walks his cat on a velvet leash each morning and raises a tiny flag on his mailbox whenever he has baked fresh bread to share.

Worked Example

Great-Aunt Rosa serves dessert before dinner, keeps forty ticking clocks each set to a different world city, and knits little sweaters for the porch chairs in winter. The family calls her eccentric with a smile, because her odd habits hurt no one and make every visit unforgettable.

Rosa's harmless, endearing oddities, from backwards meals to sweatered chairs, are exactly the kind of personal quirks the word eccentric describes.

How Eccentric Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

quirky

quirky: having odd but charming little habits

offbeat

offbeat: different from the usual in an interesting way

unconventional

unconventional: not following accepted customs

Antonyms

conventional

conventional: following accepted customs and norms

ordinary

ordinary: usual and unremarkable

How Strong Is It? — unusual → eccentric → bizarre

unusual vs. eccentric

unusual vs. eccentric: An unusual habit is merely a little different from most people's, while an eccentric one is noticeably odd and memorable.

bizarre vs. eccentric

bizarre vs. eccentric: An eccentric person strikes others as charmingly odd, but a bizarre one seems so extremely strange that people are unsettled rather than charmed.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ec-

Prefix — ec-: out of, away from (Greek ek-)

Root — centr

Root — centr: from Greek kentron, center

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: adjective-forming ending

Put it together

Put it together: Eccentric combines the Greek prefix ek-, 'out of,' with kentron, 'center,' plus the adjective ending -ic. In old astronomy an eccentric orbit was one whose path was literally 'off center,' and the word later attached itself to people whose habits sit charmingly off center from everyone else's.

Use the root in a new word: epicenter

Use the root in a new word: epicenter: News reports located the earthquake's epicenter just offshore, a word built on the same Greek root kentron, 'center,' that sits inside eccentric.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, often affectionate

Eccentric almost always describes a person, or a person's habits, as harmlessly and often endearingly odd, as in 'an eccentric aunt' or 'his eccentric routines.' It can also be a noun for the person themselves, as in 'the town eccentric,' and it carries tolerance or affection rather than alarm.
